# How to Use Midjourney on the Web: A Step-by-Step Guide

You've probably scrolled past a gorgeous AI-made image today — the kind that looks almost like a real photograph or a polished illustration. Maybe you wondered how it was made. The tool behind many of those images is Midjourney, and you don't need to be a designer to try it. Here's how to get your first image tonight, even if you've never used an AI tool before.

## What you need before you start

Midjourney is an AI image generator — you type a description (the AI calls this a **prompt**) and it draws a picture for you. Think of it as asking a very fast, very imaginative illustrator to sketch whatever you describe.

Before you jump in, two things matter:

- **An account.** You'll need a Midjourney account, which you set up with an email and password on the official website.
- **An active subscription.** Midjourney no longer offers a permanent free tier. You'll need a paid plan (Standard, Pro, or similar) to generate images. Pricing is shown clearly when you sign up, so you won't be caught off guard.

## A walkthrough on the web app

1. **Open midjourney.com in your browser** on your phone or computer. Click the **"Sign In"** button in the top-right corner of the homepage, then log in or create a new account.

2. **Head to the "Imagine" tab.** You'll find it in the left-hand sidebar on desktop, or along the bottom menu on mobile. This is your main canvas.

3. **Type your prompt** in the text box at the bottom of the screen. Be as descriptive as you like: *"a warm cafe at sunrise, soft golden light, watercolour style"* works beautifully.

4. **Tap "Submit" or press Enter.** The model (the AI's "brain") takes roughly a minute to produce four image variations arranged in a grid on your screen.

5. **Pick your favourite and upscale it.** Underneath each of the four images, you'll see a row of small buttons. Look for the ones labelled **"U1", "U2", "U3", or "U4"** — these stand for "Upscale". Tap the U-button under the image you like best, and the tool will produce a full-resolution version you can download. (Without clicking that button, the image stays at the smaller preview size.)

6. **Download your image.** Once upscaled, a small download icon appears below the larger image. Tap or click it, and the file saves to your device.

A handy tip: Midjourney's current model is noticeably better at reading longer, more detailed prompts. If you've tried it before and felt the results didn't match your words, try a fuller description this time.

## A few prompt ideas to try first

If you're staring at an empty box wondering what to type, here are some friendly starting points:

- **For a personal project:** *"a flat-lay photograph of a home office desk, morning light, plants, minimalist style"*
- **For social media:** *"a playful illustration of a dog wearing sunglasses, bold colours, cartoon style"*
- **For learning:** *"a simple diagram of the water cycle, clean infographic style, labelled"*
- **For fun:** *"a tiny astronaut riding a kangaroo across the outback, digital art"*

Once you've made a few images, try changing just one word — swap "morning" for "evening", or "minimalist" for "cosy". You'll quickly see how each small change shifts the whole picture.

## What this means for you

- **If you're a casual user or hobbyist:** This is one of the easiest moments to start playing with AI image generation. You don't need design skills — just curiosity and a willingness to describe what you imagine. Use it for birthday cards, blog headers, vision boards, or simply to surprise yourself.
- **If you're a content creator or freelancer:** Midjourney's strong prompt-following (meaning the AI listens more carefully to exactly what you write) means fewer wasted generations. Spend 15 minutes testing prompts you'll actually use for your work — cover images, social posts, mock-ups — and save your best results.
- **If you're brand new to AI image tools:** Treat this like a playground. Nothing you make is permanent. Click around, try weird ideas, and notice which words give you the strongest results. The best way to learn is by doing.

## A few things to keep in mind

The web app is polished and reliable, but like every AI image tool it can occasionally produce strange hands, odd text, or unexpected results — a quirk the community calls a **hallucination** (when the AI confidently makes something that isn't quite right). It's part of the process, not a reason to give up.

Also: images you generate are governed by Midjourney's terms of use. If you plan to use them commercially (selling prints, running ads, etc.), read the licensing rules first so you know what's allowed.

## Wrap-up

Midjourney's web app is one of the most beginner-friendly ways to make AI art right now. Pick one small idea — a scene, a mood, a style — sign up for a plan, and generate your first four images tonight. Once you see what comes back, you'll quickly get a feel for refining your prompts and making something you'd genuinely want to share.
